articles.title: Alone with the stars, lynx and wolves in ‘Empty Spain’
articles.summary: A world away from the tourist hotspots of the coast, Extremadura and Castile and León offer unpolluted skies, lower prices – and hope for the future of vulnerable wildlife.
body: A s photographed at night from a satellite, or the International Space Station (ISS), the Iberian peninsula looks encrusted with lights along its coastal edges. Madrid forms a big pulsing cluster near the centre, while surrounding hinterlands appear as something of a void. Ever fewer people live out in Castile and León and Extremadura, adjoining regions that cover much of what is known as La España Vac ía, or “Empty Spain”.

Not many visit either, or at least not compared with Barcelona and other glowing nodes of the tourist circuit. So, while the big ports and resorts struggle to manage surplus holidaymakers, there is room for plenty more out west, toward the Portuguese border. Some have been following the stars that way lately, under the auspices of an astrotourism initiative called Extremadura Buenas Noches.

A route map plotted point-to-point between optimal stargazing sites leads to distant outposts like La Siberia (so-called because it felt that remote to workers who laid down the first roads and railways in these parts) and the Corral de los Lobos, an ancient stone enclosure on a hilltop, built to trap wolves when they outnumbered the farmers and shepherds around here.
points: A world away from the tourist hotspots of the coast, Extremadura and Castile and León offer unpolluted skies, lower prices – and hope for the future of vulnerable wildlife.

articles.title: My friends are spouting conspiracy theories – what should I say? | Ask Annalisa Barbieri
articles.summary: You can be curious about others’ beliefs without compromising your own. Recently, I had a conversation with a friend who explained that her ill health was down to reasons I would describe as dubious. Taking certain supplements and changing her diet have significantly improved her health.
body: I’ve got another friend who thinks cholesterol is a lie and that we should live largely on meat (and supplements). Another went through a sugar causes cancer phase. And another is s ceptical of vaccines. Each of them may be right. They might not. We are learning more about the human body every day. But I was raised by scientists and I want to see a large-scale trial before I get outraged and change the way I live. Equally, I’m not convinced that a lightly regulated for-profit industry (supplements) is automatically more trustworthy than a highly regulated for-profit one (pharma).

I want to be respectful of their choices and the research they have done into their specific conditions, but for them to respect my beliefs too. The feeling I get is that they think they have the keys to the real intel and I’m being duped by the medical establishment. Or that I’m not a good friend because I don’t believe them.

I’m not sure how to have a respectful conversation about that. I ’d prefer to avoid it, but it comes up often. I find myself making non-committal comments such as “how interesting”. But I know, and they know, I’m sceptical.
points: You can be curious about others’ beliefs without compromising your own.

articles.title: Star Wars actor John Boyega on the day his 10-year-old school friend Damilola Taylor was killed: ‘It kept me up at night because I was just with the guy’
articles.summary: The star was just eight when his friend was stabbed. Decades on, he’s ready to talk about that day – how it shaped him, and how, as he becomes a father himself, it will shape him as a dad. “I feel a bit nervous,” confesses John Boyega, as he sits down in front of the camera.
body: On 27 November 2000, Damilola was stabbed in the leg with a broken bottle and left to die in a concrete stairwell, attacked as he walked home from an after-school club at Peckham library in south London. It took six years and three separate trials at the Old Bailey, costing a total of £16m, to secure a manslaughter conviction. His death shocked the nation not only because he was so young, but because all the suspects were also children. Boyega was one of the last people to see Damilola alive. The pair had enjoyed a close friendship since Damilola’s move to the UK from Nigeria in August of that year.
points: The star was just eight when his friend was stabbed.
Decades on, he’s ready to talk about that day – how it shaped him, and how, as he becomes a father himself, it will shape him as a dad.

articles.title: This is how we do it: ‘My mistress has complete control over me and makes me so happy’
articles.summary: LD is the submissive to Lady Alice’s dominatrix – and it has been a revelation for them both. • How do you do it? Share the story of your sex life, anonymously. I have cerebral palsy and live with my parents. Lady Alice is a delicious secret.
body: I met Lady Alice on X. We aren’t lovers or friends. She is my mistress and has complete control over me. I am hers to use however she pleases and she expects nothing less than absolute obedience. I don’t pay Lady Alice a fee, though I might pay for a service she needs such as a pedicure. These payments are “tributes”, tokens of respect and devotion.
I am 43 and use a wheelchair because I have cerebral palsy. I live with my elderly parents; they cut up my food and wash me. Lady Alice is a precious secret.

I never felt in control and hated my body. I had sexual impulses, but because I have ornamental hips that I can’t thrust and erectile dysfunction, I’m not equipped for sex in the conventional sense. I had a “friend with benefits” 20 years ago. We had two – admittedly fun – meetings that unfortunately lacked any real penetration.

In our sessions she makes me feel like there’s nothing wrong with me, as though I was simply born to kneel and be her “stress toy”. I need help cutting up food due to limited control over my fingers, but I am able to crawl and get down on my knees for Lady Alice.

articles.title: Guests Raised a Martini to Maestro Gustavo Dudamel’s Arrival at the New York Philharmonic
articles.summary: The changing of the guard at the New York Philharmonic, the oldest of America’s “Big Five” orchestras, is always a momentous occasion for the city, all the more so when the incoming music director is among the most celebrated conductors of his generation.
body: Guests were invited to don “bold black tie” attire, surely a nod to the conductor’s gift for bringing even the most stately of halls to life. That spirit—part pomp and part party, lest we forget Dudamel helped inspire the series Mozart in the Jungle —carried through the occasion.

The evening began with Venezuelan bites, including an arepa bar, on Lincoln Center’s plaza, and ended with a more traditional three-course dinner in the hall’s Grand Promenade post-performance. Rows of chairs lined the plaza’s perimeter, facing the square’s spectacular fountain. Whether intentional or not, it felt like a knowing nod to Bad Bunny’s Super Bowl shoutout to the familiar Latin family tradition of kids asleep on chairs at the function.

articles.title: At the New York City Ballet Fall Fashion Gala, Stevie Nicks and Sarah Jessica Parker Brought Down the House
articles.summary: In the 14 years since Sarah Jessica Parker established the New York City Ballet’s Fall Fashion Gala, the benefit has raised more than $40 million, drawing the biggest names across the arts, fashion, and entertainment together in support of the world-renowned dance company.
body: “It’s about revisiting something that, in your mind’s eye, is extraordinary,” the multi-hyphenate and NYCB Board Vice Chair said of the occasion: a glittering night of collaboration between some of the most prominent designers and choreographers of our time. “You watch supremely talented people come together to offer New York City one of the great, great nights at the theater.”

Thursday night’s “extraordinary” affair raised $3.45 million for the company and began even before the curtain rose on a trio of world premieres: honorary gala chair Stevie Nicks made a rare red carpet appearance (her first since the Met Gala) alongside Parker. After effectively shutting down the step-and-repeat—Parker in a balletic, hand-painted custom tulle and ribbon gown by Simone Rocha, and Nicks in a mauve Morgane Le Fay frock and flower crown—the duo joined Matthew Broderick, Nicole Ari Parker, Julia Fox, and Olivia Rodrigo for the night’s performances in David H. Koch Theater.

articles.title: For Her Fashion Week Debut, Heidi Klum’s Daughter Lou Takes a Style Cue From Mom
articles.summary: Heidi Klum and daughter Lou put their own spins on the peplum for a mother-daughter moment at Vivienne Westwood.
body: It’s hardly unusual for family members to borrow from one another’s wardrobes—or, at the very least, their styling tricks. For her first Paris Fashion Week appearance, Heidi Klum’s youngest daughter, Lou, took a sartorial cue from her supermodel mom, with the pair arriving at the Vivienne Westwood spring 2027 show in coordinating peplum silhouettes and vertiginous platforms.

The matching stopped there, however. Klum stayed true to her penchant for high-impact glamour in a sculptural white blazer with sweeping, rounded lapels, its waist cinched with gold buttons before flaring into a petal-like hem. She paired it with a matching floor-skimming column skirt and inky blue stacked platform heels. Lou, meanwhile, gave the silhouette a distinctly Gen Z spin in an acid-wash pink denim top with a raw, flared waistline and asymmetric matching miniskirt, finished with a snakeskin-print shoulder bag, and floral strapped platforms.

Beauty-wise, there was another subtle echo. Both wore their hair loose—Klum’s blonde lengths tousled around her shoulders, Lou’s brunette curls left voluminous and natural—and leaned into warm, smoky makeup.
points: Heidi Klum and daughter Lou put their own spins on the peplum for a mother-daughter moment at Vivienne Westwood.
